paper_title: Near-Optimal Rates for O(1)-Smooth DP-SCO with a Single Epoch and Large Batches
authors: Christopher A. Choquette-Choo, Arun Ganesh, Abhradeep Guha Thakurta
statement: (a) Can we obtain the same tighter batch gradient steps guarantee in Table 1, without assuming the unconstrained minimizer to be in the set C ? Informally, we only use this assumption to show the gradient norm is decreasing, i.e. the distance between xt − xt−1 is decreasing in t, and so the gradient differences ∆t are bounded by smoothness. However, if gradients remain large during training, we expect training to reach the boundary of C quickly, in which case xt − xt−1 should also be small (because the gradient step is mostly reversed by the projection into C ). Hence we believe this assumption is not required for Accelerated-DP-SRGD to achieve T = n1/4 , but we do not know how to formally show this.
